_comment: Shader effects: what the pause menu's Shaders page offers. shader_overlay.gd builds one effect per entry in this order - for screen passes, a later entry draws over an earlier one - and settings_menu.gd turns each param into a row under the shader's own heading. 'id' keys this effect's saved state in user://settings.cfg (section [shaders], keys '<id>_enabled' and '<id>_<param key>'), and 'enabled' is what a fresh install starts with. Param types: 'float' reads min/max/step (a slider row, with an optional 'suffix' shown after the value) and 'bool' is a toggle row. The uniform each param drives is the param's own 'key', so a shader's uniforms, this list and the saved keys all carry the same names. Two kinds of effect. A 'screen' effect (the default when 'kind' is absent) is a full-screen post-process: it names a 'shader', and the overlay gives it a layer of its own drawn over the frame beneath it. A 'world' effect is the geometry itself rather than a picture of it: it names no shader and gets no layer, and instead lists the 'materials' whose shaders it drives and the 'enable_key' uniform the list's switch is pushed to as 1 or 0, because a material has no visibility to hide. A world effect's params drive uniforms of those materials, and each param only has to exist on one of them - the water's ripple is declared by the water material alone - which is why the overlay warns when a param exists on none rather than on any. Where a param's unit is the screen rather than the world, its label says so: the CRT's 'picture_scale' is screen pixels per dot of the picture, not a count of lines, so a dot is always a whole number of the screen's pixels and one value means the same thing at every window size (on a 960-pixel-tall window: 1x is the frame itself, 2x is 480 lines, 4x is 240 - the raster of a late-90s set - and 8x is 120). Where a param's unit is the picture, it says that too: the CRT's mask pitch is picture pixels per phosphor triad. And where it is the world, it says blocks: the bend's radius is the distance at which the bend has bitten, in the same blocks the terrain is counted in.
